title: 第二課 Good Ways to Take Photos
subtitle: 10/21–10/22 · 課本 p.42–45

slides.title: 課文大意：什麼是 photo marathon？
points: photo marathon（攝影馬拉松）是一種 event（活動）：大家在同一天拍照。
通常有 6–8 小時的 time limit（時間限制）。
一開始拿到一份 themes（主題）清單，例如 “red”、“daily life”，每個主題拍一張。
最後 submit（提交）照片，judges（評審）選出最好的，有人會贏得 prizes（獎品）。
examples: For this event, you take photos all on the same day.
Judges look at the photos and choose the best ones.

slides.title: 課文大意：Zach 的拍照小技巧
points: 不要只拍一張，多拍幾張：You're more likely to get a good one.
試試不同 angles（角度）：low angles、high angles、side views。
只拍一個 subject（主體），而且不要放在 middle（正中間），要 put it off to the side。
不要太常用 zoom（變焦），改成 move closer（走近一點）。
清晨或傍晚拍：The light is better then.

slides.title: 重點單字（一）：活動相關
points: event (n) 活動；事件：The event starts at 9:00 in the morning.
limit (n) 限制：You have a time limit to finish.
theme (n) 主題：What is the theme of the party?
judge (n) 評審；裁判：The judge will choose the best team.
prize (n) 獎；獎品：Tom won a prize for his art.
marathon (n) 馬拉松；submit (v) 提交 → submits / submitted
slides.tip: win a prize（贏得獎品）是固定搭配，不說 get the prize 也可以但 win 最常用。

slides.title: 重點單字（二）：拍照相關
points: angle (n) 角度：She took the picture from many angles.
low (adj) 低的 ↔ high (adj) 高的
side (adj) 側面的：the side door / side view；side (n) 邊：sit on the right side
subject (n) 主體；主題：Dogs are often the subject of my photos.
middle (n) 中間：in the middle of the room
zoom (n) 焦距；變焦
slides.tip: 一字多義：subject 也是「科目」（My favorite subject is English.）；judge 也可以當動詞「評斷」。

slides.title: 片語：time limit（名詞＋名詞）
points: 前面的名詞說明後面的名詞，表示「什麼樣的限制」。
time limit 時間限制、speed limit 速限、age limit 年齡限制、weight limit 重量限制
examples: You should drive within the speed limit.
There is no age limit for this event.
They have a strict weight limit for carry-on luggage.
slides.tip: 前面的名詞用單數：a time limit，不說 a times limit。

slides.title: 片語：do one's best to + 原形動詞
points: 盡力去做某事。one's 要隨主詞改：I → my best, they → their best, he → his best。
to 後面接原形動詞。
examples: Then do your best to take great photos.
Please do your best to arrive on time.
They did their best to win the game.
slides.tip: 常見錯誤：do your best to taking ✗ → do your best to take ✓

slides.title: 句型：be more / less likely to + 原形動詞
points: likely (adj) 可能的。be more likely to + V：比較可能做…；be less likely to + V：比較不可能做…
be 動詞要跟主詞變化：I am / You are / He is
examples: You're more likely to get a good one.
Happy people are more likely to smile.
You are less likely to get sick if you exercise.
People are less likely to go out in cold weather.

slides.title: 片語：put it off to the side
points: off 是副詞「離開」，to the side 是「往旁邊」→ 從中心移到旁邊一點。
代名詞要放中間：put it / them off to the side。
examples: No. Put it off to the side. That looks better.
The box is in the way; please put it off to the side.
I don't want to eat the onions, so I'll put them off to the side.

slides.title: 句型：The ... choose the ... ones.
points: ones 代替前面提過的複數名詞（photos、students…），避免重複。單數用 one。
the + 最高級（best、bravest、nicest）+ ones：選出最…的那些。
examples: Then the judges choose the best ones.
The leaders choose the bravest ones.
The teachers choose the nicest ones.
slides.tip: good → better → best；brave → braver → bravest；nice → nicer → nicest

slides.title: 句型：My ... don't / doesn't look as ... as yours.
points: as + 形容詞原級 + as：和…一樣…；否定 not as … as：沒有…那麼…
主詞複數用 don't，單數用 doesn't；look 後面接形容詞。
yours ＝ your + 名詞（your pictures / your shoes）。
examples: My pictures don't look as good as yours.
My shoes don't look as new as yours.
My backpack doesn't look as big as yours.
slides.tip: as 中間放原級：as good as ✓，as better as ✗

lines.text: Do you like taking photos? Then you might enjoy a photo {{1}}. It is a fun {{2}}. Everyone takes photos on the same day, and there is a time {{3}} of six to eight hours. At the start, you get a list of {{4}}, like “red” or “daily life.” You must take a photo for each one. At the end, you {{5}} your best pictures. The {{6}} look at all the photos and choose the best ones. Some people win {{7}}!
Are you ready for the photo marathon, Ken?
Yes! I’m {{8}} forward to it.
{{9}} are some of the themes?
Oh, things like “red” or “daily life.”
Will the judges choose the best {{10}}?
Yes. And some people get prizes.
Then do your {{11}} to take great photos!
Your pictures are great! My pictures don’t look {{12}} good as yours.
Don’t just take one photo of something. Take a lot. You’re {{13}} {{14}} to get a good one.
So if I take only one photo, I’m {{15}} likely to get a good one?
Exactly. And don’t put the subject in the middle. Put it {{16}} {{17}} the side.
Please do your best {{18}} on time.
The teachers choose the {{19}} ones.
My backpack {{20}} look as big as yours.

explain.11: do one’s best to + V 盡力去做
explain.12: not as + 原級 + as：沒有…那麼…
explain.13: be more likely to + V：比較可能
explain.14: be more likely to + V：比較可能
explain.15: 只拍一張 → 比較不可能拍到好照片 → less likely
explain.16: put it off to the side 移到旁邊
explain.17: put it off to the side 移到旁邊
explain.18: do one’s best to + 原形動詞
explain.19: the + 最高級 + ones；nice → nicer → nicest
explain.20: backpack 是單數 → doesn’t；look as big as

sections.title: 三、新編對話：拍照小技巧

lines.text: Hi, Milo. Are you taking pictures of the flowers?
Yes. I’m joining a photo marathon next week. Can you give me some {{21}}?
First, try different {{22}}, like high ones and low ones. Get down on the ground and try a {{23}} angle.
What about taking a photo from the {{24}}, not the front?
Sure! Then your pictures will be more {{25}}.
This red flower is my {{26}}. Should I put it in the {{27}} of the picture?
No. Put it off to the side. That looks better.
The flower is far away. Can I use the {{28}}?
Don’t use it too much. Just move {{29}} to the flower.
When is the best time to take pictures?
In the {{30}} morning or the {{31}} afternoon. The {{32}} is better then.
Thanks! Maybe I’ll win a {{33}}!
Be {{34}} and do your best! Oh, wait. Your bag is {{35}}.
Sorry! I’ll put it off to the side.

explain.26: subject 主體（照片要拍的東西）
explain.33: win a prize 贏得獎品
explain.35: be in the way 擋路

sections.title: 四、圖表文意 What Do People Take Pictures Of?

lines.text: People take the most pictures of {{36}}.
About {{37}} of people probably take pictures of their meals.
Only 12% of people take pictures of {{38}}, like birthday parties.
16% of people take pictures of {{39}} when they go on trips.
The same number of people take pictures of pets and animals and of {{40}}.

explain.37: meals 餐點 → food and drinks 18%
